claims: The Jones Act is the Merchant Marine Act of 1920.
The Jones Act is a federal statute requiring that all goods transported by water between U.S. ports be carried on ships that are U.S.-flagged, U.S.-owned, U.S.-built, and U.S.-crewed.
The purpose of the Jones Act is to support U.S. maritime commerce, national security, and shipbuilding.
The Jones Act mandates U.S. ownership (75%), construction, and crewing for domestic ocean-going trade.
The Jones Act can be temporarily waived by the Department of Homeland Security if a situation is in the interest of national defense.
The Jones Act was waived in 2026 to ease oil and gas transportation following a conflict.

AP News notes that in March 2026, the Trump administration issued a 60-day waiver of the Jones Act rules to allow foreign ships to carry fuel such as gasoline and diesel between American ports to help lower energy prices during a conflict with Iran.
